contract_plain_english: After normalizing the sub-gaussian norms of X and Y to one in the proof of Lemma 2.7.7, equation (2.22) is the pair of bounds E exp(X²) ≤ 2 and E exp(Y²) ≤ 2. It does not itself include the later product bound.

source_evidence.anchor: Lemma 2.7.7 and the opening normalization sentence of its proof
source_evidence.observation: Lemma 2.7.7 assumes X and Y are sub-gaussian. Its proof says, ‘Without loss of generality we may assume that ∥X∥ψ2 = ∥Y∥ψ2 = 1. (Why?)’
The display is E exp(X²) ≤ 2 and E exp(Y²) ≤ 2. The next text says that the normalized lemma claims that if these bounds hold, then E exp(|XY|) ≤ 2.
The ψ2 norm is displayed as ∥Z∥ψ2 = inf {t > 0 : E exp(Z²/t²) ≤ 2}, which is the definition invoked by the preceding unit-norm normalization.

binders: Jointly defined real-valued random variables X and Y.
definitions_and_conventions: The conjunction in (2.22) consists of two separate marginal exponential-moment bounds.
hypotheses: The proof is in the normalization ∥X∥ψ2 = ∥Y∥ψ2 = 1.
implicit_context: Display (2.22) occurs inside the proof of Lemma 2.7.7 after unit normalization.
In the proof’s sentence-level logic, (2.22) is also written as the antecedent sufficient for the desired normalized product bound E exp(|XY|) ≤ 2.

details: Both ψ2 norms are normalized to exactly 1 before the display.
The exponent is the square of each variable with no additional coefficient.
Each expectation is bounded by the exact threshold 2.
The display contains only marginal expectations and states no independence assumption.
The numbered display itself is only the pair of quadratic exponential-moment bounds; the product conclusion appears in the surrounding prose.

undebatable_constraints: Both bounds in the conjunction must be present.
The exponents are X² and Y², and both right-hand sides are exactly 2.
The display is situated under the unit-ψ2-norm normalization.
No independence or mean-zero hypothesis is stated.
The numbered equation must not be expanded to include the surrounding product conclusion.
